cards.body:
## Summary
A Linga conversation's place in the turn is nine loose fields, and four places decide from them what the learner may do: the server's guards, the view, the phone panel and the TV's key handler. They disagree. Replace the cluster with one named turn state and one transition table in lib/english/turn.ts. The server refuses anything the table refuses, the view marks those actions disabled, and the phone and TV draw from the same answer.

## Description
conversation.ts handles leave, resume and pause before its pending and finished guards (:133-143). As a result, Space on the TV (LingaTV.tsx:54, no waiting check) pauses a turn in flight. The phone then draws an enabled Resume (LingaPhone.tsx:63). Resume clears the pending token (:134), and the model's answer arrives about 14 s later (report.md: tutor avg 14s) and is thrown away as 409 by checkCurrent (:38, :191). The learner's reply and its evidence are lost. The TV hides this because LingaTV.tsx:75 disables actions from waiting in the component, not in the view. For the same reason the view's phone list offers an enabled finish while pending (view.ts:419), which the server refuses (:142) and the phone's own button disables (:73): three answers to one question. The view sweep that should catch this swallows every 409 (linga-rules-test.cjs:319) and has no pending, moment or coaching fixture. There are 75 flag reads in 5 files. Every new Linga control (the next card on this deck adds reuse detection to the turn) has to reproduce the right conjunction in each of them.

## Flow
- turn.ts (pure, no React): turnState(c) -> preparing | unprepared | waiting | paused | moment | coaching | quiz | your-turn | finished, with the precedence written once. ACCEPTS: Record<TurnState, action[]> plus the one data guard (coach needs a learner reply). accepts(c, action). refusal(c, action) gives the learner sentence.
- conversation.ts: after the episode and command-id checks, one guard: if (!accepts(c, action)) throw ConversationError(refusal, 409). The scattered state guards (:142-144, :168, :173) go. The lastTurnId staleness check stays.
- view.ts: the talk branch switches on turnState. Every action that runs a conversation command carries disabled: !accepts(c, action). answerOf and spoken.blocked read the state.
- LingaPhone.tsx: the talk panel switches on turnState, and its buttons take disabled from accepts. LingaTV.tsx: Space sends pause only when accepts(c, 'pause').
- Gates: cd desk && npm test (linga-rules-test, uat-surface-test, typecheck) exit 0.

## Expected impact
An in-flight reply can no longer be thrown away by a pause and a resume. Anything the TV, the phone or the LT driver is offered in a state, the server accepts in that state, and the sweep proves it. The next Linga turn feature changes one table instead of four flag chains.

## Evaluation
Claim: one turn state and table makes the server's refusals and the view's offers agree, and a turn in flight survives Space and Resume
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard cases pass (2 guards green by design); 75 flag reads in 5 files; 3 counted disagreements (pause/resume during a pending turn, finish offered while refused, pause accepted on a finished rehearsal)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: Taught phrases come back: the next scene invites one, code sees it reused
acceptance: case 1: learner record with taught [A: fix 'I has booking' -> 'I have a booking', from an earlier rehearsal, never reused; B: already reused] -> command('start') sets conversation.review.id === A.id, the stub engine's opening prompt JSON carries bringBack.phrase === 'I have a booking' with an instruction to invite it and never say it, and A.offered becomes 1 (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs, engine stubbed)

case 2: during that scene, an unsupported reply 'Hi, I have a booking for Friday.' -> getLearner().english.taught A has reusedAt set, reusedIn === the conversation id and reusedQuote === 'I have a booking', and conversation.review.used holds the learner's words; decided by review.ts (normalised containment), not by the model (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

case 3: the same reply sent (a) after the starter rung made it supported, or (b) after the partner's own line already contained the phrase -> no reuse recorded: reusedAt stays unset (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

case 4: lingaView on linga-recap with review.used -> the hero is the comparison picture 'Linga taught · <earlier scene title>': 'I have a booking' beside 'You said it tonight': <the learner's words>, the arch shows the star-burst ('done'), and viewText carries both quotes. With review offered but not used -> the recap holds 'I have a booking' as its one sentence to take with you, and the counts stay in the data line (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

case 5: withholding - on linga-talk with review set and not yet used, JSON.stringify(lingaView(s)) (TV row, phone list, caption, hero) does not contain 'I have a booking'; the phrase reaches a screen only after it is used or on the recap (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

case 6: a taught item offered in two scenes without being reused is not due a third time -> the next start picks the next unused item, or sets review null when none is left (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)
case 7: cleanEnglish round-trip -> keeps offered, reusedAt, reusedIn and reusedQuote on a taught item, and drops a taught item whose reusedAt is not a number (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

case 8 GUARD: a learner with no taught items -> conversation.review is null and the opening prompt has no bringBack key; the moment cases (exact quote, spacing, beginners two per rehearsal) and ladder cases 1-7 stay green (tools/linga-rules-test.cjs)

cards.rollback: The series is test(linga) then feat(linga). Reverting the feat commit removes review.ts and the start, turn and recap wiring. The new Taught fields are optional, so a learner file written while the feature was in reverts cleanly: cleanTaught's old field list simply drops offered and reusedAt on the next load. Conversation.review is optional on the session and is ignored by the old view.
cards.runner_up: A replay that counts: the reply to a replay question is unsupported unless help was used (today conversation.ts:207 forces supported:true on every replay and view.ts:326 says so), so coached language can earn independent evidence (UAT theme 3).
cards.body:
## Summary
Linga stops a scene to teach one thing, keeps it in the learner's record (up to 60) and never uses it again. Make those taught phrases come back. When a new scene starts, code picks one phrase that is due, and the partner is asked to create a moment where the learner would naturally need it, without saying it. Code checks each unaided reply for the phrase. The recap then shows it as a picture: what Linga taught in an earlier scene next to the words the learner used tonight.

## Description
Today a moment is written to learning.taught (conversation.ts:198) and read in exactly one place, a collapsed list on the phone's map (LingaPhone.tsx:52). The tutor never sees it (context(), :57-64), and the reply right after a moment is marked supported (:201). So nothing ever shows whether a fix held. The design names this step, 'Next visit: a new setting calls for an earlier skill; spaced review' (LINGA-CONVERSATION-DESIGN.md:57), and the last UAT runs miss it: 3 of 3 J4 Characters had no independent success, 4 of 4 J3 recaps had only counts and no language to reuse, and Petra's finding asks to notice 'whether the learner can reuse the correction just taught'. All the data is already stored. Code decides and the model only phrases: review.ts picks the due item (from an earlier rehearsal, not yet reused, offered fewer than twice, oldest first) and judges reuse (normalised containment in an unsupported reply, not counted when the partner already said the phrase in this scene). The tutor is only told to create the opening. Withholding holds: the phrase is on no screen during the scene. It appears only once used, or on the recap as the sentence to take away.

## Flow
- start: review.ts dueTaught(learning) -> Conversation.review {id, kind, better, fromTitle}. Taught.offered += 1. The opening and every turn prompt carry bringBack {phrase, meaning} with 'invite it, never say it'.
- turn: after validation, reusedIn(reply, review, c) runs in code. On a hit, taught[id] gets reusedAt, reusedIn and reusedQuote, and c.review.used gets the learner's words. Model evidence and achievements are untouched (AG-2: no score).
- recap (TV, Open Door): used -> the comparison hero, 'Linga taught · <earlier scene>' next to 'You said it tonight', with the star-burst in the arch. Not used -> the recap's one sentence card holds the phrase to take away. The caption stays under 25 words and the counts move to the data line.
- phone: the recap list and My map mark a phrase 'used again' with the scene it was used in.
- persisted-shape consumers (all in-tree): types.ts, placement.ts cleanTaught, rules.ts cleanEnglish, conversation.ts, view.ts, LingaPhone.tsx, and store.ts load (spreads the conversation; no change needed). The fixture at tools/tv-keys-test.cjs:252 (taught: []) is unaffected.
- Gates: cd desk && npm test exit 0, and a Playwright capture of the recap in both states on a second dev server (webpack, seeded DESK_DATA_DIR).

## Expected impact
The learner can see whether something they were taught stayed with them. They meet it again unprompted in a new place and see it on the TV when they use it. The recap stops being a set of counts. Direction: this adds a capability the context description does not name (review across scenes). It falls within the description's scope (error moments, the tutor conversation) and within the design's own 'Next visit' row.

## Evaluation
Claim: taught phrases are picked, invited, detected in code when reused unaided, and shown as a picture on the recap, without ever being put on screen during the scene
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard cases pass (1 guard green by design); taught read in 1 place (a collapsed phone list), 0 decisions
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction
